section_summary: This section follows the allocation, pricing, sale and shipment of Japanese cotton textiles after the war, including disputes over Philippine purchases and Netherlands Indies prices. It also records plans for raw cotton procurement, Indian requests for a share of Japan’s imports, and the proposed transfer of textile sales from the U.S. Commercial Company to occupation authorities. The final pages contain a request for consular help with claims and the beginning of an enclosed sales contract.

subfiles.title: Recommended allocation of Japanese cotton textiles
subfiles.from: Henry G. Harper, Combined Textile Committee
subfiles.about: Recommends country allocations for 120 million yards of Japanese cotton textiles.
subfiles.summary: Allocates textiles among Burma, French Indochina, Hong Kong, the Netherlands East Indies, the Philippines and Siam according to civilian needs.

subfiles.title: Reply on textile allocation
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the committee’s allocation recommendations.
subfiles.summary: Thorp says distribution is proceeding and the recommendations will be followed where financial and other considerations permit.

subfiles.title: Revised recommendation for Burma
subfiles.about: Revises Burma’s proposed mix of Japanese cloth and yarn.
subfiles.summary: Because of urgent clothing needs, Burma should receive mostly cloth; yarn should comprise 10–25 percent of its allocation.

subfiles.title: Commerce transmittal of Wallace letter
subfiles.about: Forwards the Secretary of Commerce’s reply to the Textile Export Association.
subfiles.summary: Henry sends Wallace’s comments on exports of Japanese cotton textiles.

subfiles.title: Commerce response to Textile Export Association
subfiles.about: Explains allocation authority, pricing and reasons for exporting Japanese textiles to Far Eastern markets.
subfiles.summary: Wallace describes the proposed 120-million-yard allocation, generally accepted pricing based on U.S. export ceilings, and the need to supply textile shortages, including in the Philippines.

subfiles.title: Objection to Japanese textile prices
subfiles.about: Questions U.S. market pricing for Netherlands Indies textile allocations.
subfiles.summary: Zimmerman argues that American price levels and markups may burden purchasers and hinder recovery of essential exports from the Netherlands Indies.

subfiles.title: Reply on textile price policy
subfiles.about: Explains the U.S. Commercial Company’s uniform pricing policy.
subfiles.summary: Phillips directs Zimmerman to the company for price discussions and says American export prices offered a uniform basis that was often below Far Eastern market prices.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of pricing explanation
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the explanation of Japanese textile prices.
subfiles.summary: Zimmerman says he need not discuss the matter with Arthur Gardiner at present.

subfiles.title: Offer to publish Textile Mission report
subfiles.about: Offers the Textile Research Institute’s help printing the Textile Mission to Japan report.
subfiles.summary: Jacobs asks about printing delays and proposed circulation.

subfiles.title: Reply on Textile Mission report distribution
subfiles.about: Reports that the Textile Mission to Japan report has been printed and distributed.
subfiles.summary: Martin says 25,000 copies were printed and further publication is unnecessary.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Japanese rayon reparations
subfiles.about: Questions a press report describing proposed reparations from Japan’s rayon industry.
subfiles.summary: Rose asks whether an article repeats errors from Pauley’s earlier report.

subfiles.title: Reply on rayon reparations policy
subfiles.about: Clarifies the status of unreleased U.S. reparations policy.
subfiles.summary: Martin says the current policy paper differs from Pauley’s report and that press accounts are unofficial.

subfiles.title: Request for additional report copies
subfiles.about: Asks whether more courtesy copies of the textile report are available.
subfiles.summary: Jacobs seeks copies for Institute members.

subfiles.title: Reply on courtesy copies
subfiles.about: Offers reasonable additional courtesy copies of the textile report.
subfiles.summary: Martin confirms that more copies can be supplied.

subfiles.title: Proposed notice on Philippine textile sales
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of an attached notice to the American Embassy.
subfiles.summary: Foster cites exporters’ protests over sales of Japanese textiles to the Philippines.

subfiles.title: Proposed cable on Philippine textile demand
subfiles.about: Describes Philippine sales, pricing and a request for future demand estimates.
subfiles.summary: The draft seeks an estimate of Philippine interest in 1947 purchases from Japan or Germany.

subfiles.title: Airgram to Manila on Japanese textiles
subfiles.about: Requests Philippine purchasing estimates amid concern about competition with U.S. textiles.
subfiles.summary: The airgram describes allocations and asks about additional demand from Japan or Germany.

subfiles.title: Manila airgram on textile market prices
subfiles.about: Reports Philippine textile prices and market conditions.
subfiles.summary: The damaged OCR preserves a price table and discussion of textile scarcity and demand, but much of the analysis is unreadable.

subfiles.title: Instructions to SCAP on trade and raw materials
subfiles.about: Addresses British textile payments, Indian cotton pricing and other Japanese trade matters.
subfiles.summary: The telegram also mentions private financing and Australian wool procurement.

subfiles.title: Tokyo acknowledgment
subfiles.about: Acknowledges State’s March 5 telegram.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo says action is pending and a reply will follow.

subfiles.title: Manila report on reluctance to buy Japanese cloth
subfiles.about: Reports Philippine reluctance to accept contracted Japanese cotton cloth.
subfiles.summary: Trading agencies fear losses against current American textile prices and probably want no additional cloth.

subfiles.title: Inquiry on Philippine textile contracts
subfiles.about: Seeks reasons for Philippine reluctance and information on shipments.
subfiles.summary: State relays USCC’s questions about contracted and additional textiles and asks when shipments will occur.

subfiles.title: Instructions on claims for Japanese textiles
subfiles.from: Arthur Z. Gardiner, U.S. Commercial Company
subfiles.about: Requests consular assistance with claims concerning Japanese cotton textiles sold to the Philippines.
subfiles.summary: Gardiner explains old stock and new production contracts, asks the consul to identify qualified textile inspectors, and sets out notice, inspection and timing rules for claims. He also requests reports on the imports’ reception and local market effects.

subfiles.title: Senator Overton’s inquiry on foreign cotton
subfiles.about: Forwards a constituent’s protest against U.S. funds buying foreign cotton for occupied mills.
subfiles.summary: Overton asks for an early report on procurement policy.

subfiles.title: Agreed revisions to Overton reply
subfiles.about: Records revisions agreed by Generals Hilldring and Noce.
subfiles.summary: The proposed reply would favor available U.S. cotton and seek self-supporting occupied economies.

subfiles.title: War Department recommendations on Overton reply
subfiles.about: Recommends stronger language in the State Department’s reply to Senator Overton.
subfiles.summary: Noce proposes U.S. cotton procurement where available and maximizing occupied-area exports.

subfiles.title: Earlier draft reply to Senator Overton
subfiles.about: Explains proposed cotton procurement policy for Germany and Japan.
subfiles.summary: The draft acknowledges other cotton exporters’ market rights while describing U.S. interests and the need for reasonably priced raw materials.

subfiles.title: Revised reply to Senator Overton
subfiles.about: States revised U.S. cotton procurement policy for occupied areas.
subfiles.summary: The revised text says specified U.S. funds will buy American cotton when suitable supplies are available and seeks self-supporting economies in Germany and Japan.

subfiles.title: Indian invitation to SCAP cotton representatives
subfiles.about: Invites two SCAP representatives to New Delhi for cotton discussions.
subfiles.summary: India proposes talks with McDermott and Toppens during their return to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Reply to Indian invitation
subfiles.about: Reports forwarding India’s proposed visit to occupation authorities.
subfiles.summary: State says it recommended favorable consideration.

subfiles.title: SCAP report on electrical goods
subfiles.about: Reports wartime delivery of electrical goods consigned to Prague.
subfiles.summary: The shipment went through the German Embassy in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Manila explanation of textile reluctance
subfiles.about: Explains Philippine objections to Japanese textile prices and deliveries.
subfiles.summary: Manila cites falling U.S. prices, financing limits, uncertain shipping and quality, and reluctance to order another 15 million yards.

subfiles.title: State position against contract cancellation
subfiles.about: Declines to support Philippine cancellation of its Japanese textile contract.
subfiles.summary: State relays USCC’s objections and asks for Embassy comments.

subfiles.title: Japanese textile program accounts
subfiles.about: Corrects payment and unpaid invoice totals for Japanese textiles.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum compares accounts as of April 15 and April 18 and identifies a partial Philippine contract payment.

subfiles.title: Finished versus gray cotton textiles
subfiles.about: Explains customary finishing allowances and proposes Japanese contract terms.
subfiles.summary: Walmsley addresses yardage, seconds, shrinkage and pricing adjustments.

subfiles.title: Current U.S. bleached flannel prices
subfiles.about: Compares New York flannel quotations with the Japanese textile program price.
subfiles.summary: Henry finds comparable U.S. flannel may be exported below USCC’s 37-cent price.

subfiles.title: Japanese cotton textile production estimates
subfiles.about: Compares Japanese production estimates with reported January–February output.
subfiles.summary: Barton identifies major discrepancies affecting sales commitments and urges a teleconference to verify inventory. An attached table lists production by swatch number.

subfiles.title: Available yardage for New York offer
subfiles.about: Lists Japanese cotton piece goods potentially available for a New York offer.
subfiles.summary: The estimate totals about 130.8 million linear yards for shipment by July 31.

subfiles.title: Conversation on Philippine textile purchase
subfiles.from: R. R. Ely, Department of State
subfiles.about: Records discussion of Philippine contract payment and possible credit.
subfiles.summary: Gardiner says the contract will stand but Philippine officials seek credit; an RFC loan offset is being considered.

subfiles.title: Manila recommendation to cancel contract balance
subfiles.about: Recommends permitting cancellation of the remaining Philippine textile contract.
subfiles.summary: Manila reports local surpluses, worsening government finances, distribution problems and declining attractiveness of the deal.

subfiles.title: Reply to Representative Gearhart
subfiles.about: Explains U.S. policy on cotton procurement for Germany and Japan.
subfiles.summary: The text says U.S. funds will procure suitable American cotton when available while respecting other exporters’ interests and seeking self-supporting occupied areas.

subfiles.title: Distribution of occupation-area textile cables
subfiles.about: Addresses distribution of textile cables to relevant agencies.
subfiles.summary: The mission proposes sending copies to White of Agriculture and Claxton of State.

subfiles.title: Proposed amendment to CCC cotton contract
subfiles.to: War, Agriculture, USCC and State officials
subfiles.about: Proposes rules for sales of Japanese textiles in convertible currencies.
subfiles.summary: The amendment would protect USCC and CCC repayment from currency conversion proceeds and other dollar exports.

subfiles.title: Query on alleged British interference
subfiles.about: Requests the basis for a complaint about British interference with Japanese textile marketing.
subfiles.summary: State says the unresolved issue concerns payment terms and describes the British position as patient.

subfiles.title: Congressman Boggs forwards cotton protest
subfiles.about: Forwards a telegram concerning delayed cotton purchases for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Boggs asks for a report.

subfiles.title: Newburger telegram on cotton purchase delay
subfiles.about: Urges resolution of a delay in purchasing American cotton for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Newburger disputes a currency conversion issue and asks Boggs to help secure immediate purchase.

subfiles.title: USCC proposal to transfer cotton programs
subfiles.from: John D. Goodloe, U.S. Commercial Company
subfiles.to: Secretaries of State, War and Agriculture
subfiles.about: Seeks approval to transfer Japanese and German textile program functions to occupation authorities.
subfiles.summary: Goodloe gives sales and collections figures and proposes an October 1 transfer of all USCC functions, including cotton shipping, to SCAP and OMGUS. The attached July 10 letter from Arthur Gardiner to Roland Hartman records earlier discussions and proposed staffing assistance.

subfiles.title: State reply deferring transfer approval
subfiles.about: Defers formal approval of USCC’s withdrawal from cotton programs.
subfiles.summary: State accepts the need for withdrawal but awaits consultation with occupation commanders on the effective date.

subfiles.title: Alternative draft reply to Goodloe
subfiles.about: Proposes deferring the October 1 transfer until occupation authorities are ready.
subfiles.summary: The draft asks War to consult commanders in Germany and Japan.

subfiles.title: India’s request for additional cotton quota
subfiles.about: Requests an additional Indian raw cotton export quota for Japan.
subfiles.summary: India accepts a future 45 percent share but seeks an extra 349,000 Indian bales to address exports lost since the war.

subfiles.title: State reply on Indian cotton procurement
subfiles.about: Explains U.S. plans for financing and sourcing Japanese raw cotton imports.
subfiles.summary: State distinguishes near-term procurement from later purchases expected to use an export-import revolving fund. It favors commercial sourcing by Japanese spinners over fixed national quotas and considers India’s requested quantity too large relative to estimated total needs.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Japanese textile imports into the United States
subfiles.about: Asks whether Japanese cotton textiles may be imported into the United States.
subfiles.summary: Hope requests permissible textile types, quantities and cotton origins.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of amended Japanese cotton agreement
subfiles.about: Sends a signed agreement removing USCC from the Japanese cotton textile program.
subfiles.summary: Goodloe says the agreement also provides for the program’s continuation.

subfiles.title: Request to retain consular assistance with textile claims
subfiles.from: Peter A. McDermott, SCAP Foreign Trade New York Office
subfiles.about: Asks whether U.S. consuls may assist with claims under new old-stock textile contracts.
subfiles.summary: McDermott says claims have been rare but the new sales contract needs a provision for consular assistance.

subfiles.title: Supplemental textile contract terms
subfiles.about: Sets supplemental acceptance and claims terms for Japanese cotton textiles.
subfiles.summary: The form limits new-production claims and clarifies treatment of old-stock loss and shipment notices.

subfiles.title: Japanese cotton textile sales contract
subfiles.about: Sets sales, inspection, rejection and claims procedures for Japanese cotton textiles.
subfiles.summary: The form defines old stock and new production textiles, contract schedules, buyer inspection rights and the treatment of SCAP determinations. It begins the provisions for old-stock claims, including notice and inspection, and continues beyond page 73.
